title: NAS 410 Audit Documentation for Tulsa MRO and Suppliers
description: Tulsa repair stations and suppliers: NAS 410, Nadcap AC7114 and Part 145 NDT records prepared for your Responsible Level 3 to approve. Contact us today.
h1: NAS 410 Audit Documentation for Tulsa Repair Stations and Aerospace Suppliers
html:
Tulsa's repair stations, engine and component shops and aerostructure suppliers often answer to the FAA, an airline customer and a Nadcap assessor in the same year, and each one reads the NDT personnel files. Atlantis NDT is the ASNT NDT Level III consultant behind those files: we prepare and review your NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audit documentation, and your Responsible Level 3 approves what we produce. Describe your audit to us and we reply within one business day.

Start here: Atlantis is not your Responsible Level 3

Under NAS 410, the employer designates a Responsible Level 3 in writing, and that person holds authority over the whole qualification and certification program: the written practice, the training, the examinations, the examiners and every outside agency the company relies on. Atlantis is not your Responsible Level 3 and will not be named as one. We do not certify technicians to NAS 410, and we run no NAS 410 courses or examinations. The certification on each inspector's file is your company's decision, issued under your written practice.

That boundary is not a formality. A repair station or supplier that lets a consultant's name drift into the role on paper ends up with a program nobody inside the company can defend at audit. We work underneath the person who owns the program: reading documents, finding gaps, drafting replacements, sorting personnel files and rehearsing the audit. Each of those outputs is a recommendation until your Responsible Level 3 signs it. The national service description is on the NAS 410 audit compliance documentation page, and the role itself is discussed under aerospace Responsible Level III.

Tulsa's maintenance economy

American Airlines moved its technical operations headquarters from LaGuardia to Tulsa in 1946, and the base marked eighty years in 2026. American describes Tech Ops Tulsa as the largest commercial aircraft maintenance facility in the world: 3.3 million square feet of hangar and shop space on 246 acres at Tulsa International Airport, nearly 5,000 team members, and around 400 aircraft passing through each year. The work spans airframe overhaul, component repair and engine overhaul, including CFM engines.

Engines are a Tulsa specialty beyond the airline. Lufthansa Technik Engine Services, the former BizJet, has worked in Tulsa since 1986 and overhauls Rolls-Royce Tay 611-8 and 611-8C engines used on corporate jets. Manufacturing is here too. The former Spirit AeroSystems plant in Tulsa became part of Boeing when that acquisition closed in December 2025, and NORDAM and L3Harris appear among the aerospace suppliers in the Tulsa and Oklahoma City cluster. Down the turnpike, the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex at Tinker Air Force Base employs more than 9,400 people and anchors military depot maintenance, while Kratos is building a plant in Bristow to produce GEK turbojet engines with GE Aerospace.

That combination means a Tulsa NDT technician might inspect a wheel under a manufacturer's manual on Monday and a machined detail under a prime's specification on Thursday. The personnel rules behind those two jobs are not the same, and an auditor will ask which rules applied to which work.

Three audits a Tulsa shop can face in one year

AuditWho runs itMain documentsWhat it reads in NDT files
FAA surveillance of a Part 145 repair stationThe FAA14 CFR Part 145, the repair station and quality control manuals, the approved training programWhether inspection personnel meet the program the FAA accepted, and whether training is recorded
Customer or airline supplier auditThe customer's quality staffThe contract, the customer's maintenance requirements and often NAS 410Written practice, certifications by method, vision, examinations and technique approvals
Nadcap NDT assessmentA Nadcap assessor working for the Performance Review InstituteAC7114 baseline and method slash sheets, plus customer requirementsSampled personnel files and process records, line by line

Nondestructive testing at a repair station sits under a limited rating, and the FAA's own guidance notes that the United States has no national certification for NDI personnel, so certification stays employer-based. Our Part 145 repair station NDT page covers the manual and training-program side in detail. Where a contract adds NAS 410, the shop's written practice has to satisfy it on top of everything the FAA expects, and the files must prove both.

Where NAS 410 enters a repair station

Most Tulsa repair stations do not adopt NAS 410 because they want to. It arrives in a customer contract, a purchase order for component work or a manufacturer's requirement, and then it binds. From that point, the minimum training hours, experience, examinations, vision checks and recertification intervals in the standard become obligations the customer can audit. The repair station still performs the inspection tasks exactly as the manufacturer's NDT manual describes them. What changes is the evidence that the person doing the task was properly qualified.

The friction usually shows up in four places. The written practice was written for the FAA program and never mentions NAS 410 at all. Inspectors hold method certifications but no record of the specific examination on the hardware they actually test. Training was delivered on the job but logged as a single line with no course outline. And nobody can say who the Responsible Level 3 is, because the person once named has retired or moved to another base. We trace each of those gaps to the clause it fails and draft the fix for your Responsible Level 3 to approve. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison helps teams who learned their trade under ASNT documents.

Engine, wheel and component shops: the eddy current and penetrant load

Component and engine work in Tulsa leans heavily on eddy current and fluorescent penetrant inspection, with magnetic particle on steel landing-gear and actuator parts and ultrasonics where a manual calls for it. Each method generates records an auditor can follow from the shop floor back to the file. For eddy current, that means reference standards with certificates, probes and instruments identified on the work record, and certifications that cover the technique used, whether bolt-hole, surface or wheel inspection. For penetrant, it means the daily checks on the line, the light readings at the inspection booth and the material checks, all on file for the shift when the part was inspected.

Interrupted service catches many maintenance shops. Technicians rotate between tasks and bases, and a person certified in eddy current can go months without performing it. The written practice has to say what counts as an interruption and what the person must do to return to work in that method, and the records must show it happened. We check the roster against work records for exactly this. Method background for local teams is on eddy current testing in Tulsa, penetrant testing in Tulsa and ultrasonic testing in Tulsa, and calibration tracking is covered in equipment past calibration.

Aerostructures and defense depots: the manufacturing side of Tulsa NDT

The maintenance story is only half of Tulsa. Tulsa has a long-established aerostructures plant, formerly operated by Spirit AeroSystems, and machine shops, sheet-metal houses and finishing lines around the city feed that kind of production. Inspection there looks more like a build-side Nadcap shop than a repair station: penetrant and magnetic particle lines running to process specifications, eddy current at fastener holes, and ultrasonics on bonded or machined details. The auditor's interest moves from maintenance-manual tasks to process control, technique approvals and the prime's specification revision on each order.

Depot work adds a third pattern. Suppliers and contractors near the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex at Tinker can receive military contracts whose NDT clauses name NAS 410 or a service-specific requirement. A shop that serves a commercial airline, an aerostructure prime and a depot customer may need to show three different flow-downs met by one written practice. We sort those requirements into a single flow-down matrix: each line is a customer clause, and the next column shows the paragraph of your written practice that answers it. When a contract changes, the matrix shows exactly what must be revised and what can stay. Your Responsible Level 3 approves the matrix along with the written practice it supports, and the written practice for aerospace page explains how we draft the underlying document.

Outside-agency Level 3 arrangements, put in writing

Plenty of Tulsa shops are too small to employ a Level 3 in every method, so they contract one. NAS 410 allows the Responsible Level 3 to be provided by an outside agency, and it allows outside agencies to deliver training or examinations when the written practice provides for it. What it does not allow is an informal arrangement. The agreement should state the scope of authority, the methods covered, how the person reviews and approves documents, how often they are on site, how examinations are administered and graded, and who keeps the records.

Atlantis does not act in that capacity for clients, but we review these agreements against the standard and the written practice, and we check that the outside agency's own qualifications are on file. When an outside instructor or examiner is involved, their qualification evidence belongs in your records, not only in theirs. The same thinking applies to any lab you use for overflow work, which our subcontractor approval audits page covers.

Revision 6 in a maintenance setting

NAS 410 Revision 6 came out in December 2025, released by AIA with Accuris. It clarifies certification requirements and introduces Appendix D, which sets out a points system for Level 2 personnel seeking to sit the initial Level 3 examination, with credit earned for defined NDT activities. Senior Level 2 technicians at a large maintenance base may have done exactly the kind of work that earns credit, from writing work instructions to supervising trainees. Whether any of it counts depends on how your Responsible Level 3 adopts Appendix D and on whether the activity was ever recorded against the person's name.

Repair stations should also plan the transition itself. Your customers and your written practice decide when the change takes effect, guided by the transition wording in the standard. Revise the written practice, course outlines and examination question banks as one package, then brief the FAA program owner so the repair station manuals and the NDT documents stay consistent. Background on what changed is in NAS 410 explained.

How Atlantis supports Tulsa shops

Atlantis works from Houston and Hyderabad, and Tulsa is within driving distance of Houston for site work. A typical engagement starts with a remote gap review of the written practice and a sample of files, continues with drafts and a findings list your team works through, and ends with a site visit for a mock audit: pulling files the way an assessor does, comparing work records with certifications, and asking inspectors to explain the technique they just performed. If findings arrive after the real audit, we help assemble the cause analysis and the evidence that the fix works.

Shops that also do industrial work under ASNT documents can keep a separate program for it; the Level III of record in Tulsa page covers that model for SNT-TC-1A work. Regional context sits on NDT consulting in Tulsa, aerospace NDT in Tulsa and NDT consulting in Oklahoma. Suppliers with work across the Red River may also find the Dallas NAS 410 documentation page useful.

What to send us

  • The NDT written practice, plus the repair station manual sections that describe NDT, if you hold a Part 145 certificate.
  • The current Responsible Level 3 designation and any outside-agency agreement.
  • The contracts, purchase orders or customer requirements that invoke NAS 410 or name a Nadcap requirement.
  • Your NDT roster by method and level, with certification, recertification and vision dates.
  • Complete files for two technicians, including one who moves between bases or tasks.
  • A month of work records for one method, so certifications can be checked against the work actually done.
  • Your most recent audit findings and responses.

Tulsa audit-readiness checklist

  1. The written practice names NAS 410 wherever a contract invokes it, and states the revision.
  2. The Responsible Level 3 appointment is current and signed by the employer.
  3. Each certification lists the method, level and the techniques the person actually performs.
  4. Specific examinations reflect the hardware the shop inspects, and the papers are kept.
  5. Interrupted service is defined, tracked and closed out for every affected person.
  6. Training records carry course outlines, hours and instructor qualifications.
  7. Vision checks, including color perception, are inside the interval the written practice sets.
  8. Records are kept for as long as the written practice and the customer require, as outlined in aerospace NDT records retention.

faq.q: Can Atlantis be named as our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: No. Atlantis does not accept that designation. NAS 410 lets your company appoint an employee or a Level 3 provided by an outside agency it contracts with; we prepare and review the documents that person approves.

faq.q: Will Atlantis certify our technicians to NAS 410?
faq.a: No. The certificate is issued by your company through its own written practice. We neither teach NAS 410 courses nor administer NAS 410 examinations. What we do is test whether each file would support the certification your company signed.

faq.q: We hold a Part 145 certificate. Why would NAS 410 apply to us?
faq.a: Because a customer contract or purchase order invokes it. Part 145 sets the FAA framework, and many airline and manufacturer customers add NAS 410 for NDT personnel. See Part 145 repair station NDT.

faq.q: Does NAS 410 change how we perform an inspection from the manufacturer's manual?
faq.a: No. The task follows the manual. NAS 410 governs how the person performing it is trained, examined, certified and kept current, and the records that prove it.

Your written practice defines it, within what NAS 410 requires. It covers a technician who has not performed a method for a stated period and sets what they must do before returning to it. Auditors check that the rule is applied, not just written.

faq.q: Can an outside agency provide our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: Yes, NAS 410 allows it, but the arrangement must be written down with a clear scope. Atlantis does not take that role. We can review the agreement and the agency's qualification records against your written practice.

faq.q: Do you visit Tulsa, or is everything remote?
faq.a: Both. Reviews and drafts move by secure file share, and a Level III drives up from Houston for personnel-file checks and the rehearsal audit. The two Atlantis offices are in Houston and Hyderabad; there is none in Oklahoma.

faq.q: How should a repair station prepare for NAS 410 Revision 6?
faq.a: Read the transition wording, confirm your customers' dates and revise the written practice, course outlines and examination banks together. See NAS 410 explained.

faq.q: Can you help with our response to audit findings?
faq.a: Yes. We help work out the cause and gather objective evidence; your company writes and submits its response. See aerospace NDT corrective actions.

faq.q: Does Atlantis hold Nadcap accreditation or an FAA repair station certificate?
faq.a: Neither one. The repair station certificate and any Nadcap accreditation discussed in your audit are held by your company, not by Atlantis.
